interface.title: Country Flow — Panel designer · BD FACSCanto II
interface.stage_of_work: Experiment planning (designing the staining panel before acquisition) and recording it in the notebook
interface.what_it_is_for: Pick surface markers from the lab's own antibody inventory and have them automatically assigned to the panels and detectors of a 7-colour FACSCanto II. The assignment avoids conflicts, keeps backbone markers fixed, works around the PI live/dead stain and skips unusable vials. The design is then exported as a printable figure and a per-detector CSV.

data.source: built-in example catalog, then uploaded test files (edge-case-catalog.csv, example-catalog.csv)
data.note: Started on the built-in example catalog (68 antibodies: 31 human, 37 mouse). Then imported edge-case-catalog.csv, which replaced the catalog with 15 antibodies because the catalog held only example rows. The import skipped 2 rows that lacked a marker or fluor, and flagged 1 BUV737 row as 'no detector'. Later, after Clear catalog had emptied it, re-imported example-catalog.csv (68 antibodies). Downloaded files: SM009-PBMC-surface-screen_2026-10-31_panels.csv, the matching .png, country-flow-catalog-2026-10-31.csv and country-flow-catalog-template.csv.

features.name: Constraint-aware channel assignment board
features.general: Pick items from an inventory and have a solver place each into a slot of one of several fixed-slot containers. It avoids forbidden slots and unusable stock, and shows the result as one table per container with warnings.
features.specific: Search the antibody catalog and add markers. The solver assigns each to Panel A/B/C × FACSCanto detector (FITC, PE, PerCP-Cy5.5, APC, APC-Cy7, Pacific Blue, AmCyan) and lists reagent, clone and location. It shows 'Things to check' and 'No usable reagent' notes.
steps: type a marker in Search your catalog
click a suggestion or press Enter
read the panel/detector placement in the panel tables and the marker list
remove a marker with × or Clear all markers
serves_tasks: Choose the targets to measure and see them assigned to channels automatically
Check that the design respects which reagents are actually usable

features.name: Pin an item to the same slot in every container (backbone)
features.general: Flag an item as shared, so it occupies the same slot in every container and the slot count updates.
features.specific: Press Backbone on a marker. It gets the same fluor on all panels, tagged 'backbone', and the slot counter rises (e.g. 9 of 12 → 11 of 12).
steps: add the marker
press its Backbone toggle
check that every panel shows it in the same detector with a backbone tag
serves_tasks: Keep reference markers identical across all tubes

features.name: Capacity overflow banner with one-click fix
features.general: When the requested items exceed total slot capacity, show which item did not fit and how many containers are needed, with a button that adds one.
features.specific: Red banner 'more fluors than there are available channels for 2 panels. Add another panel?' names the unplaced marker. The 'Add Panel C' button re-solves the design. The Add panel and Remove panel buttons do the same by hand.
steps: add markers beyond capacity
read the error and the unplaced marker
press Add Panel C (or Add panel)
optionally Remove panel to see the error return
serves_tasks: Resolve a design that needs more channels than the instrument has

features.name: Global assay option that reserves a channel and steers the solver
features.general: Toggle an assay-wide option that reserves one slot in every container and makes the solver avoid a conflicting slot, with a warning when it cannot.
features.specific: Include PI for live/dead reserves PerCP-Cy5.5 on every panel and steers markers away from PE. If PE is still used, a 'PI spills into PE' warning appears. Unchecking it frees the channels (12 → 14 slots for 2 panels).
steps: check or uncheck Include PI for live/dead
watch PI rows appear or vanish and markers move between PE and other detectors
read the PI-spill warnings
serves_tasks: Choose the targets to measure and see them assigned to channels automatically

features.name: Inventory table with inline edit and stock status
features.general: Keep a reagent inventory with per-item status and expiry. Filter it, add, edit or delete rows with in-page confirmation, and export it. Changes flow straight into the planner.
features.specific: Antibody catalog table with All/Human/Mouse filter and text filter. Edit and Add antibody forms (Status In stock/Low/Out, Expires) show expired dates in red. Delete and Clear catalog ask for confirmation in the page. Download catalog CSV, Blank template and Load example rows are also here.

Edit a row's status and Save changes
Add antibody for a missing marker
Delete a row and confirm
Download catalog CSV

features.name: Spreadsheet import with row validation
features.general: Load an inventory from a CSV file, skipping incomplete rows and tagging items no slot can hold, and report what was loaded, skipped and flagged.
features.specific: Import CSV replaces the catalog if it holds only example rows, otherwise appends. It skips rows lacking a marker or fluor, tags fluors no detector reads as 'no detector', and reports counts in a toast.

pick a CSV file
read the toast (loaded, skipped, 'no detector')
clear the filter to review the imported rows

features.name: Notebook record export (figure + tidy CSV)
features.general: Turn the finished design into a printable summary figure with metadata, plus a long-format CSV with one row per container × slot.
features.specific: Export record shows a preview with run date, operator, species, viability, panel count, panel cards and notes. Download CSV gives columns experiment, run_date, operator, instrument, species, panel, detector, laser_filter, marker, fluor, backbone, clone, vendor, catalog_number, lot, location, expires and viability. Download figure (PNG) and Print figure are also available (print output not observed).
steps: press Export for notebook
type Operator and press Today for the run date
check the preview
press Download CSV / Download figure (PNG) / Print figure
